articles.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts as architects of tumor immune geography and lymphoid organization
Calpain-mediated TBP cleavage disturbs neuronal AMOT-YAP1 signalling
articles.abstract: Abstract The transcription factor TATA-box-binding protein (TBP) plays a crucial role in neurons, as highlighted by its involvement in spinocerebellar ataxia type 17 (SCA17), where pathological polyglutamine expansions disrupt its function. While the molecular pathomechanisms remain unclear, our previous study showed that calcium-activated calpains cleave TBP in SCA17 cell and animal models. Here, we pinpoint a major calpain cleavage site after residue T106, C-terminal to TBP’s polyglutamine tract. The resulting polyglutamine-containing N-terminal fragments mislocalise to the cytoplasm and exhibit increased aggregation. Both the N-terminal and the nuclear-localised C-terminal fragments contribute to calpain overactivation. SCA17 cell line-based multi-omics analyses revealed that TBP fragments alter pathways linked to neuronal function and neurodegeneration, identifying AMOT as a key player. Further analyses in SCA17 cell lines, patient-derived fibroblasts and induced neurons as well as in rat and zebrafish models confirmed AMOT’s pivotal role in neurons, regulated by TBP and mediated via YAP1-dependent signalling. These findings offer further insights into TBP’s neuronal function and suggest broader implications of AMOT for neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental disorders.

articles.title: Two functionally distinct amyloid-β intermediates link aggregation pathways to pathology in Alzheimer’s disease
articles.abstract: Abstract Neurotoxic intermediates formed during amyloid-β (Aβ) aggregation are thought to drive Alzheimer’s disease, yet their rarity and transient nature have obscured their identity and formation pathways in the human brain. Here, we combine super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule functional imaging with kinetic modelling to classify Aβ intermediates according to their membrane-disrupting activity and connect their damaging effects to the aggregation pathways that generate them. Applying this framework to recombinant Aβ42, an Alzheimer’s knock-in mouse model and human Alzheimer’s brain tissue, we find two functionally distinct intermediate populations present across all systems. They form through separate aggregation routes and differ in their neurotoxicity, abundance and susceptibility to inhibition. Both damage neurons and glia, but only one converts into plaques. Suppressing these intermediates pharmacologically in mice reduces plaque burden, attenuates astrogliosis and improves cognition. Our findings connect model systems with human pathology and identify intermediate formation pathways as actionable therapeutic targets across protein-misfolding disorders.

articles.title: Single-cell machine learning uncovers genetically anchored, cell-type specific programs of Alzheimer’s disease
articles.abstract: Abstract Univariate differential expression analysis dominates single-cell transcriptomic studies of Alzheimer’s disease, yet marginal testing alone cannot resolve multivariate disease-associated structure or distinguish clinical from neuropathological signatures. Here we introduce TriSCOPE, a framework integrating multivariate predictive modeling, donor-aware differential expression, and pseudotime inference, applied to six Alzheimer’s disease snRNA-seq datasets comprising ~4.2 million nuclei from 627 donors. Across six major brain cell types and 41 subclusters, we identify cell-type-specific predictively expressed genes that are largely non-overlapping with differentially expressed genes, revealing disease-relevant signals invisible to univariate approaches. Conditional GWAS–eQTL colocalization anchors a subset of these predictively expressed genes to inherited Alzheimer’s disease risk loci, including 27 genetically supported gene–cell type pairs (among them ARL17B , JAZF1 ) with no significant differential expression. Integration across all three analytical branches nominates high-confidence convergent programs including astrocytic stress markers (such as GFAP , MT2A ), neuronal signaling genes (like RASGEF1B , LINGO1 , NRG1 ), and microglial and oligodendrocyte regulators (including SYTL3 , SPP1 , APOD ). Comparison of clinical and neuropathological models reveals cell-type-specific divergence between cognitive and pathological Alzheimer’s disease signatures. Key predictively expressed genes including ARL17B , LINGO1 , and APOE replicate across independent cohorts, with cross-cohort generalizability confirmed across all three analytical branches of TriSCOPE.

articles.title: Absolute quantification and profiling of cellular tRNAs by nanopore sequencing and a deep learning classifier
SimPoly: Simulation of polymers with machine learning force fields derived from first principles
Repeated loss of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet’s Amundsen Sea sector during late Pleistocene interglacials
articles.abstract: Abstract Sea-level reconstructions and numerical models suggest that the vulnerable West Antarctic Ice Sheet underwent major mass losses during the late Pleistocene, raising global sea level by several metres. However, direct evidence from ice-sheet proximal records for such retreat has remained inconclusive. Here we investigate variations in clay mineral assemblages and past ocean temperatures archived in West Antarctic continental margin sediments during the last 800,000 years. Our results demonstrate that the supply of glacigenic detritus sourced from the main outlet glaciers in the Amundsen Sea sector of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet ceased almost entirely during all previous warm periods, documenting the loss of their drainage basins. Concomitant seawater warming, revealed by a microfossil proxy, is attributed to intensified deep-water advection towards Antarctica’s Pacific margin, which is corroborated by the clay mineralogical evidence. Our findings show that ocean forcing can drive major deglaciation of West Antarctica and related global sea-level rise.

articles.title: Electrode-associated growth reveals structure of OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires in anaerobic methanotrophic archaea
articles.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic methanotrophic (ANME) archaea are key regulators of methane emissions in anoxic environments, yet their physiology remains poorly understood due to the lack of axenic cultures. Here, we show that cultivation on poised electrodes yields near-axenic cultures (95.8% relative abundance) of a freshwater ANME, for which we propose the name ‘ Candidatus Methanoperedens vercellensis’. We identified key physiological properties of ‘ Ca . M. vercellensis’: doubling times of 4.6 days at 30 °C, menaquinone as respiratory electron carrier, the inability to oxidize ethane, and preferential reduction of iron oxides over nitrate after cultivation on electrodes. A 3.3 Å cryo-electron microscopy structure of filaments displayed on the archaeal surface revealed polymerized OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires, which are homologous to OmcZ nanowires essential for long-range (>10 μm) extracellular electron transfer (EET) in Geobacter sulfurreducens . The archaeal OmcZ-type nanowires include dense, collinear stacking of protected hemesakin to bacterial OmcZ nanowires, but with post-translational modification, thus yielding morphology distinct from bacterial OmcZ nanowires. Notably, in contrast to bacterial OmcZ, archaeal OmcZ-type nanowires do not form interconnected networks, and hemes are less solvent-exposed, which can protect them from the environment. Surprisingly, these archaea assemble OmcZ into nanowires even in the apparent absence of prolyl isomerase involved in folding bacterial OmcZ. This work establishes a model system for molecular understanding of nanowire-mediated EET in archaea.

articles.title: The transcriptional regulator IκBζ is essential for ILC2 effector functions
articles.abstract: Abstract Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2) are the sentinels that ensure tissue homeostasis and engage in the immune response to helminths by secreting type 2 cytokines. Here we show that IκBζ, an atypical member of the IκB family, controls basal IL-5 production by ILC2s and governs their effector program during helminth infection and asthma. Peripheral ILC2s express IκBζ at steady state, and its expression is further induced upon stimulation with IL-33 or IL-25 in an NF-κB- and STAT3/5-dependent manner. Upon activation, IκBζ refines chromatin accessibility at regulatory elements of effector cytokine loci, thereby licensing transcription. Due to reduced type 2 cytokine secretion and impaired proliferative capacity of ILC2s, mice with IκBζ-deficient ILC2s show delayed clearance of the hookworm Nippostrongylus brasiliensis and reduced papain-induced airway inflammation. Taken together, our study highlights the central role of IκBζ in orchestrating the ILC2 effector program in different tissues in health and disease.

articles.title: Reply to: Comment on “Self-organizing neuromorphic nanowire networks as stochastic dynamical systems”
LLM ensemble PREVIA predicts future PTSD risk from emergency department trauma narratives with expert-level accuracy
Correlative nanoscale chemical imaging reveals delocalized Faradaic processes at isolated MXene flakes
articles.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) combine an electrochemically active surface with high conductivity and hydrophilicity, which makes them a unique class of materials for electrochemical applications. While the pseudocapacitive behaviour of MXenes in acidic environments is relatively well understood on macroscale electrodes, intrinsic electrochemical phenomena occurring on single MXene flakes remain unclear. Here, we use scanning X-ray microscopy (SXM) to correlate the electronic structure of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene flakes at the nanoscale with local electrochemical reactions triggered at the sub-flake level by scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM). For several proton-coupled electron transfer reactions, including electrochemical oxidation and the hydrogen evolution reaction, we demonstrate a delocalization of the reactions well beyond the MXene flake area in contact with the droplet cell. Furthermore, we show evidence of hydrogen storage on monolayer MXene flakes. This work highlights fundamental insights into the role of interfacial water on surface redox reactions.

articles.title: Evidence and measures of the digital usage divide from 40 million Windows devices
articles.abstract: Abstract Digital infrastructure is crucial for economic opportunities, social inclusion, and civic participation, but benefits remain unevenly distributed. Existing measures, such as computer ownership and broadband adoption, do not capture the depth and variety of digital use. We develop measures using Microsoft telemetry collected during operating system updates from 40 million Windows devices in U.S. households. These measures provide greater coverage and granularity than existing commercial or government surveys. Device representations at the ZIP-code level reveal substantial variation in usage, including an urban-rural divide and disparities within narrowly defined Metropolitan Statistical Areas. Income and education correlate with these differences. These effects are large and suggest that digital usage gaps extend beyond the local availability of essential IT infrastructure. The findings call for interventions that complement infrastructure access with support for technology use and skills development. The resulting indices are publicly available to support future research on digital inequality.

articles.title: Hydration water drives elastin’s entropic elasticity
Crystal records of erupted vs. trapped magma in volcanic arcs
articles.abstract: Abstract Arc andesites are hybrids generated by mixing of mafic and silicic magmas. The silicic endmember can contribute to crustal growth or trigger explosive eruptions, yet remains difficult to constrain due to limited representation in the erupted record. Here, we show that textural, elemental and isotopic records preserved in plagioclase can distinguish between trapped and erupted crystal mush, thus constraining conditions of magma storage vs. eruption in arc systems. We define the plagioclase eruptibility field, a narrow and recurrent anorthite range (An~61) that represents erupted melt across Central Andes volcanoes upon mafic recharge. The recycled plagioclase cargo is dominantly An~43, recording prolonged crystallisation and assimilation within silicic mushes. This pattern repeats in continental and composite arcs globally, indicating strong eruptive filtering of arc magmas and widespread occurrence of dormant felsic and mafic mushes that, in most cases, contribute to crustal growth; yet exceptionally, felsic mushes can rapidly remobilise to generate super-eruptions.

articles.title: Archival and palaeoenvironmental documentation of extreme climate events reveals generational amnesia in collective memory
articles.abstract: Abstract Collective memory shapes how societies respond to extreme climate events, yet long-term evidence on how the collective memory of such events becomes perceptually biased over time is lacking. Here, we utilise four centuries (1470–1900) of climatic archives from northern China, along with tree–ring–based hydroclimate reconstructions, which are validated against instrumental observations of Wet/Dry Index (1901–2000) to fill the gap. We find that historical records reveal systematic, non-random mismatches, where severity assessments are often biased toward recent experience rather than absolute climatic anomalies. Correlations between historical and natural records increase when the natural series is re-standardised using 20–40-year sliding windows, reflecting a generational offset. A heuristic agent-based model reproduces this pattern, suggesting that generational amnesia is sufficient to explain the offsets in perception of environmental change. We argue that historical archives carry a generational imprint of perceptual bias, in which the severity of climate extremes is judged against recent lived experience rather than long-term climate variability. This has implications for bias-aware corrections for risk assessment, adaptation, and paleoclimate reconstruction.

articles.title: Nanometer-resolution imaging of living bacteria across species and cellular orientations
articles.abstract: Abstract The bacterial cell envelope is a complex superstructure that is an important target and a major barrier for antibiotics. To date, highest-resolution images of native cell envelopes have been obtained by atomic force microscopy (AFM), but its use is limited by challenges in bacterial immobilization. We establish glutaraldehyde-functionalized glass surfaces for reversible covalent attachment, enabling robust adhesion across species and cellular orientations while preserving cell viability and growth. This approach allowed imaging of Escherichia coli both expressing O-antigen and fully lacking lipopolysaccharide (LPS) oligosaccharides, revealing that AFM contrast depends on LPS complexity and confirming previously observed outer membrane domains as LPS-enriched islands. It also enabled imaging of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii outer membranes, which lack the characteristic protein trimers observed in model E. coli . Finally, we discovered growth-phase dependent alterations in E. coli pole morphology, where trimer networks typical of exponential-phase cells were unresolved and morphological defects appeared.

articles.title: Comment on “Self-organizing neuromorphic nanowire networks as stochastic dynamical systems"

Enhanced CO2 Storage Capacity and Hydrate
Formation Kinetics Using SDS-Stabilized CO2 Emulsions for
Submarine Carbon Hydrate Storage
articles.abstract: Abstract Surfactant-assisted CO2 emulsion injection into cold aquifers offers enhanced CO2 storage capacity and accelerated hydrate formation. However, prior studies have largely treated surfactants as either emulsion stabilizers or hydrate kinetic promoters in isolation, leaving unresolved whether the concentration that optimizes CO2 trapping is compatible with that needed for hydrate formation near submarine temperatures. This study addresses that gap through a systematic, multiscale evaluation of SDS-stabilized CO2 emulsions. At ∼3 °C, SDS precipitates before reaching its critical micelle concentration; solubility, interfacial tension, and bulk hydrate formation experiments identify 1000 ppm as a practical upper limit for porous-medium experiments. High-pressure, low-temperature microfluidic experiments show that SDS above 500 ppm improves CO2–water displacement efficiency by increasing effective CO2-phase viscosity and reducing interfacial tension, yielding smaller CO2 ganglia and stable, piston-like displacement. SDS up to 1000 ppm shortens induction times and increases hydrate film growth rates, following a power-law dependence on subcooling with an exponent of 2. CO2 emulsions further sustain open transport pathways via continued CO2 dissolution, enabling efficient long-term CO2-to-hydrate conversion. These results define a concentration window where SDS simultaneously enhances CO2 storage and hydrate kinetics.

articles.title:
High-Throughput
Fingerprinting of Polymer Biodegradation
across Phylogenetically Diverse Microorganisms
articles.abstract: Abstract With the growing accumulation of plastic waste, focus has been directed toward biodegradable polymers; however, understanding their performance across diverse microbial communities requires species-level degradation data, which throughput-limited studies of undefined or limited consortia have only partially provided, preventing the cross-species and cross-polymer comparisons driving mechanistic understanding. This work presents an integrative framework fingerprinting polymer biodegradation across phylogenetically diverse microorganisms. A modified high-throughput clear-zone assay was adapted to physiologically diverse species through minimal media formulations and used to characterize fragmentation across 19 microorganisms and 14 commercial polymers. Paucimonas lemoignei, Priestia megaterium, and Pseudomonas stutzeri showed expansive fragmentation capability. Poly(1,4-butylene adipate), degraded by 11 of 19 species, proved most universally degradable, while poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate), poly(ε-caprolactone), and poly(lactic acid) were degraded more selectively. Plate-based screening of protease, esterase, and urease activity supported the aliphatic-ester selectivity pattern. MicroResp quantification, addressing the often-conflated distinction between fragmentation and mineralization, confirmed mineralization in 63.3% (19 of 30) fragmentation-positive pairs. Comparative genomics identified 465 depolymerase homologues, 187 with predicted signal peptides. Distinct strategies─P. lemoignei’s four near-identical PhaZ paralogs versus P. stutzeri’s divergent broad-substrate α/β hydrolases─explain their comparable polyester breadth. Overall, this framework establishes a foundation for systematic accumulation of microbial biodegradation fingerprints.

articles.title:
Dipole Polarization
Engineering Enables Ultrahigh
One-Step Hydroxyl Radical Generation for Low-Chemical Water Decontamination
articles.abstract: Abstract Hydroxyl radicals (•OH) were key radicals for the removal of organic contaminants from water. Peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation had attracted broad interest as a route to •OH generation because of its asymmetric O–O bonds and ease of storage and transport. However, conventional Fenton-like activation of PMS typically produced •OH through a two-step pathway involving sulfate radicals (SO4•–), which incurred kinetic losses and limited •OH availability. Here, we reported a one-step •OH generation pathway from PMS enabled by synergistic polarization effects. This electronic regulation increased the O–O bond dipole moment from 0.45 to 3.86 D and produced a steady-state •OH concentration more than 2 orders of magnitude higher than those reported for representative state-of-the-art Fenton-like systems. Mechanistic analyses revealed that the amplified dipole promoted heterolytic O–O bond cleavage, thereby bypassing the SO4•– intermediate and enabling direct •OH generation. This system achieved efficient removal of diverse organic pollutants and increased rate constant of oxidant activation by 175–400% higher than the values reported for representative PMS/PDS-based Fenton-like systems. Life cycle assessment further revealed a lower environmental footprint, attributed to improved chemical utilization rates. This oxidant-centered strategy provided a promising route to utilize dipole polarization for efficient generation of •OH, with the potential to achieve scalable and low-carbon advanced oxidation water remediation.

articles.title:
Interaction
Between Siderite and Goethite Regulates
Fe(II) Speciation and Sustains Reduction Capacity
articles.abstract: Abstract Fe(II) drives many reduction reactions in aquifers, and its reactivity is governed not merely by total abundance but also by its speciation. Siderite is a major reservoir of structural Fe(II) and frequently occurs in close proximity with goethite. But whether such close proximity effects transformation of structural Fe(II) remains unclear. This study demonstrated that coupling siderite dissolution and diffusive transport established a narrow microenvironment between siderite surface and bulk solutions, which has higher aqueous Fe(II) (Fe(II)aq) concentration and increased pH. Close proximity enables goethite to access the microenvironment and form the proton-mediated feedback interaction with siderite, promoting the formation of surface-associated Fe(II). Therefore, the surface-associated Fe(II) pool in mixed systems increased to 109.3–538.7 μM, 2.8–13.7 times higher than that in dual-chamber systems. This increase can be quantitatively predicted from siderite surface area (A) and proton activity (aH+) via a unified relationship (A·aH+0.37). The A determines the number of available reaction sites, and the aH+ governs the reaction rate. Nitrobenzene reduction experiments revealed that surface-associated Fe(II) pool sustained reduction capacity over successive reaction cycles by linking structural Fe(II) and Fe(II)aq. These findings identify interaction between siderite and goethite as an overlooked mechanism for generating a persistent surface-associated Fe(II) pool. The species distribution of Fe(II) determines the durability of abiotic natural attenuation in aquifers.

articles.title:
Multiomics:
TBPH Enhances Thyroid Hormone Synthesis
via PIS-LPI-ERK-EGR1 Pathway
articles.abstract: Abstract Bis(2-ethylhexyl)-tetrabromophthalate (TBPH), a high-production-volume novel brominated flame retardant (NBFR), has been shown to perturb thyroid hormone synthesis, yet the underlying molecular mechanism remains poorly understood. Using transcriptomics, phosphoproteomics, and metabolomics as discovery tools, combined with validation in Sprague–Dawley (SD) rats and human thyroid follicular epithelial cells (Nthy-ori 3–1), we investigated this mechanism. TBPH increased thyroglobulin (TG) and thyroid peroxidase (TPO) in rat thyroid and elevated circulating triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) levels. In Nthy-ori 3–1 cells, TBPH remodeled glycerophospholipid metabolism, leading to phosphatidylinositol synthase (PIS)-dependent accumulation of the signaling lipid lysophosphatidylinositol 18:1 (LPI_18:1). LPI 18:1 selectively activated the ERK-EGR1 signaling axis and drove TG/TPO upregulation. Knockdown of PIS or EGR1, or pharmacological inhibition of ERK, abolished TBPH-induced TG/TPO expression. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized PIS-LPI-ERK-EGR1 pathway through which TBPH enhances thyroid hormone synthesis, highlighting a lipid metabolism-driven mechanism of endocrine disruption and providing a mechanistic basis for reassessing the health risks of NBFRs.

articles.title:
Prenatal Per- and
Polyfluoroalkyl Substances and Body
Mass Index Trajectories in Childhood: Application of Multiphase Growth
Mixture Models across the ECHO Cohort
articles.abstract: Abstract We examined the associations of prenatal per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) exposures with body mass index (BMI) trajectories and growth parameters in the Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes Cohort. Maternal PFAS concentrations (perfluorohexanesulfonic acid [PFHxS], perfluorooctanesulfonic acid [PFOS], perfluorooctanoic acid [PFOA], perfluorononanoic acid [PFNA], perfluorodecanoic acid [PFDA], perfluoroundecanoic acid [PFUnDA], and N-methyl perfluorooctane sulfonamidoacetic acid [NMFOSAA]) were measured in serum or plasma during pregnancy. BMI trajectories and growth parameters were estimated using multiphase growth mixture modeling. Among 1,125 children ages 1–9.5 years, we identified a typical BMI trajectory (n = 998, 89%; reference group) and an atypical BMI trajectory characterized by early and rapid BMI increases (n = 127, 11%). Maternal PFOA (adjusted risk ratio [RR] = 1.22 per doubling; 95% CI = 1.05–1.41) and PFOS (adjusted RR = 1.14; 95% CI = 0.99–1.32) concentrations were associated with a higher risk of atypical trajectory membership. A doubling in maternal PFOA concentrations was associated with an earlier age at adiposity rebound by 19 (95% CI = 4–33) days. Other PFAS concentrations were not significantly associated with the atypical trajectory or adiposity rebound. In this pooled cohort study, higher prenatal exposure to certain PFAS was associated with a greater risk of an obesity-related growth trajectory and earlier adiposity rebound.

articles.title:
Harvesting Corrosion
Energy for Self-Powered Gravity-Driven
Membrane Filtration and Fouling Regulation
articles.abstract: Abstract Decentralized water treatment requires low-cost technologies that can remove dissolved metal ions while maintaining stable water production without external energy input. Here, we developed a soil-mediated corrosion-current hydrogel filtration system (SCHFs) that integrates a conductive adsorptive hydrogel membrane with a soil-based corrosion-energy-harvesting unit. Natural soil served as the solid electrolyte, while discarded Al and carbon cloth enabled direct harvesting of corrosion energy for conductive-membrane regulation during gravity-driven filtration. In 60-day continuous river water filtration, the SCHFs permeate concentrations of Cu2+ and Mn2+ approaching the detection limit under the tested conditions. In addition, SCHFs also accelerated NH4+-N stabilization and reduced the final permeate concentration to 0.2 mg L–1. Moreover, a thicker but more porous surface cake layer was formed during SCHF operation, limiting pore blockage and reducing the 60-day flux decline. Microbial community analysis further indicated that SCHFs reshaped the membrane biofilm and enriched taxa associated with nitrogen transformation. Soil and electrode analyses suggested that Al released from the sacrificial electrode was partly immobilized as aluminum-containing silicate minerals, suggesting a low secondary environmental risk under controlled Al input. These results suggest that coupling soil-mediated microcurrent in SCHFs regulate interfacial transport and fouling-layer architecture, thereby improving dissolved-metal retention and long-term hydraulic stability.

articles.title:
Patterns
and Mitigation of Large Language Models’
Hallucinations on Environmental Regulatory Facts
articles.abstract: Abstract With increasing adoption of large language models (LLMs) in the environmental education, research, and policy domains, reducing hallucinations─where LLMs confidently produce wrong or fabricated results─remains a critical challenge toward trustworthy agentic AI. We evaluated hallucinations on 505 environmental water, air, and solids regulatory facts collected from U.S., China, the European Union (EU), and the World Health Organization (WHO). Across four open-weight and three commercial state-of-the-art LLMs evaluated in both English and Chinese, open-weight models hallucinated on 50–70% of facts, while commercial models hallucinated on only 7–15%. We discovered a deep geographic and linguistic imbalance, where LLMs hallucinate much less on U.S. facts, and when prompting in English. Although models were less confident on average when hallucinating, a non-trivial fraction of incorrect answers were still produced with high token-level confidence. Causal tracing identified layers where restoring the subject representation most strongly recovered correct answers, with patterns differing across models. Retrieval-augmented generation effectively mitigated hallucination, even for small open-weight models. Safe deployment of AI in high-stakes environmental workflows therefore requires both targeted mitigation of training biases and robust external knowledge grounding.

articles.title:
From
Correlation
to Causation: A Hybrid Physics-Data
Approach with Double Machine Learning for Interpretable Phosphorus
Regulation in Water Systems
articles.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) optimization, yet black-box models often suffer from physical inconsistency and poor interpretability, causing overprediction and operational risks. This study develops a hybrid physics-data-driven framework (Phys-VMD-BiTCN-iTransformer) to enhance reliability of effluent total phosphorus (TP) prediction and control. By leveraging Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Bidirectional Temporal Convolutional Network (BiTCN) for spatiotemporal feature extraction, and improved Transformer (iTransformer) for long-term dependency modeling, the framework integrates operational data with seven mechanistic features derived from ASM2d and physical laws. To transition from correlation to causality, a Double Machine Learning (DML) framework was implemented. Causal inference identified Aeration Tank 1 Dissolved Oxygen (AT1 DO) and Hydrolysis Tank 1 Oxidation–Reduction Potential (HT1 ORP) as primary drivers of effluent TP fluctuations. Based on these insights, an 8-tier staged DO adjustment strategy was developed; scenario analysis showed the effluent TP compliance rate increased from 36.1% to 58.7%, while reducing exceedance risk and unnecessary energy and chemical costs. The framework bridges deep-learning architectures with practical engineering logic. By providing interpretable causal pathways and a reliable control coefficient (K = 0.15), this research offers a scalable solution for intelligent, sustainable water systems.

articles.title:
Electrochemical
Recycling of Spent Lithium-Ion Battery
Cathodes: Direct Regeneration, Electrochemical Leaching, and Selective
Separation
articles.abstract: Abstract Growing volumes of spent lithium-ion batteries challenge waste management and resource security. Conventional recycling recovers metals but often consumes energy and chemicals while sacrificing cathode structural value. Electrochemical methods enable cathode repair, controlled dissolution, and selective recovery, yet their suitability for diverse feeds and product requirements remains unclear. This Critical Review develops a material-state- and product-oriented framework linking cathode degradation, electrochemical transformations, and product specifications. Relithiation, defect repair, and cell-level rejuvenation are evaluated as regeneration strategies, with functional repurposing considered separately. Electrochemical leaching is classified by direct or indirect redox transfer, while paired or coupled operation is treated as reactor-level integration. Electrodialysis, electrosorption, and electrodeposition are assessed for ion redistribution, selective capture, concentration, and product formation. Because extraction efficiency alone cannot establish successful recycling, we emphasize feedstock tolerance, selectivity, Faradaic and ion-transport efficiencies, energy and reagent consumption, component durability, and qualified-product yield within defined system boundaries. Future priorities include diagnosis-guided routing, realistic black-mass validation, standardized reporting, scalable reactors, and integrated techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. Electrochemical technologies can complement established recycling through feedstock-adaptive pathways that retain, recover, or upgrade cathode value.

articles.title:
A Supervised and
Visualization-Enabled Toolkit for
Robust DNA Reference Database Construction in eDNA Biomonitoring
articles.abstract: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA) and DNA-based technologies are increasingly used for biodiversity assessment, but their taxonomic resolution depends strongly on the quality, completeness, and interoperability of reference databases. Public barcode repositories often contain heterogeneous sequence lengths, inconsistent taxonomy, redundant records, and incomplete metadata, and existing tools do not always provide supervised curation, visual inspection, controlled database extension, and multiformat export in one workflow. Here, we present MFRefData (Multi-Format Reference Database), a Python-based toolkit for constructing customized reference databases using a paired CSV–FASTA architecture. MFRefData integrates NCBI sequence retrieval, primer-specific in silico PCR, standardized taxonomic annotation, VSEARCH-based dereplication, rule-based filtering, controlled database extension, visualization, and export to multiple commonly used compatible formats. Using the Pearl River fishes under standardized input conditions, MFRefData retrieved more sequences and covered more species than the refdb and CRABS toolkits, while also achieving higher sequence retrieval efficiency and memory efficiency. In an in silico mock community of 40 fish species and three mitochondrial 12S primer sets, MFRefData produced more correct species-level assignments than databases generated by the refdb and CRABS toolkits. Applied to real eDNA samples, MFRefData recovered broader species-level biodiversity signals. Overall, MFRefData provides a supervised, visualization-enabled, and multiformat framework for improving reference database transparency, technical quality control, and reproducibility, while supporting more reliable species-level taxonomic assignments in DNA-based biodiversity assessment.

articles.title:
Dual
Regulation of Monomer Transport Enables Ultrahigh
Mg2+/Li+ Selectivity in Polyamide Nanofiltration
Membranes
articles.abstract: Abstract Nanofiltration membranes are promising for lithium recovery from salt-lake brines, yet their Mg2+/Li+ separation performance can be further improved. Here, we present an organic-phase engineering strategy that systematically tailors the carbon-chain length of alkane solvents, from n-hexane (C6) to 2-methylundecane (C12), to simultaneously regulate piperazine enrichment at the water–organic interface and trimesoyl chloride diffusion kinetics. This dual regulation transforms conventional rapid and random interfacial polymerization into a more confined and homogeneous growth process. The resulting polyamide membranes exhibit a reduced negative surface charge and a narrower and more uniform pore-size distribution. These structural features substantially enhance Mg2+/Li+ separation, with the C12 membrane achieving a Mg2+/Li+ selectivity of up to 306.6 in the mixed-salt solutions. To assess performance under realistic conditions, a two-pass nanofiltration process was evaluated using simulated salt-lake brine. The C12 membrane increased lithium purity from 2.4% to 97.7% while reducing the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio from 40 to 0.024. This study provides new insight into the kinetic regulation of interfacial polymerization through organic-phase engineering and demonstrates an effective membrane design strategy for high-selectivity lithium extraction from complex brines.

articles.title:
Novel
Multi-Isotope Am and Cm Signatures Trace Temporal
Changes in Nuclear Inputs in a Baltic Sediment Core
articles.abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic radionuclides have been present in the environment since 1945 due to civil and military uses of nuclear energy. This study represents an extensive characterization of Am and Cm isotopes (241Am, 242mAm, 243Am, 244Cm, 245Cm, 246Cm), and 237Np, in a Baltic Sea sediment core directly impacted by discharges from the Studsvik nuclear research facility (Sweden). Distinct isotopic signatures were identified throughout the sediment core, enabling discrimination between inputs from atmospheric nuclear weapons testing (1952–1965), Sweden’s nuclear-weapons-related activities during the 1970s, and subsequent releases associated with civil nuclear-energy development. The findings demonstrate that higher actinides provide powerful isotopic fingerprints for resolving complex nuclear contamination histories and attributing release sources in environmental archives. This study further establishes the utility of actinide isotopic tracers beyond U and Pu and presents the first environmental application of the 243Am/241Am ratio in a system with well-constrained inputs from distinct nuclear sources.

articles.title: Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation

Nonlinear Ozone-Phytoplankton-Sea-Ice
Coupling Regulates
Fine-Scale Gaseous Elemental Mercury Enhancement in the Arctic Marginal
Ice Zone
articles.abstract: Abstract Arctic marginal ice zone (MIZ) is a key summertime source of elevated atmospheric gaseous elemental mercury (GEM), but controls on its spatial variability remain unclear. Multiscale spatial statistics, machine learning, and quantile regression were applied to MOSAiC in situ observations (June-September 2020). GEM exhibits strong fine-scale spatial autocorrelation at 10 km (Moran’s I = 0.876). Random forest model (R2 = 0.85) with SHAP attribution identified ozone (O3), chlorophyll a (Chla), and open water fraction (OWF) as dominant GEM predictors. Quantile regression revealed that nonlinear coupling among OWF, Chla, and O3 strengthens under high GEM concentrations. By further combining spatial analysis with quantile regression modeling, a GEM-sensitive region was identified (OWF = 0.156–0.404, Chla = 1.17–1.57 μg/L, O3 = 9.2–19.7 ppb); within this region, both the O3 × Chla and O3 × OWF interactions exhibited significant positive correlations. The positive effect of O3 × Chla persists across all regions, while the O3 × OWF coupling varies dynamically with the retreat of sea ice. O3 indirectly favors GEM accumulation via regulating phytoplankton, and sea-ice melt exerts stage-dependent modulation of atmospheric oxidizing capacity. This study identifies O3 as a critical MIZ mercury regulator, and embedding O3-mediated pathways in models improves GEM projections under Arctic warming.

articles.title:
Occurrence
and Environmental
Weathering of Agricultural
Microplastics on Beaches across Japan: Insights into Surface Mineralization
and Metal Binding
articles.abstract: Abstract We investigated the coastal occurrence and environmental weathering of microplastics derived from polymer-coated fertilizers (PCFs) across Japan. A field survey along the Japanese coastline revealed that PCF-derived microplastics are widely distributed on beaches throughout the country, indicating that agricultural microplastics have dispersed far beyond agricultural landscapes. Compositional analysis showed that these particles consist predominantly of polyolefins (∼70%) and polyurethanes (∼30%) and commonly exhibit oxidative degradation accompanied by iron enrichment. Bulk elemental analysis demonstrated positive correlations between iron and multiple heavy metals. Micro-X-ray fluorescence mapping using a focused 20-μm beam showed that chromium is heterogeneously distributed on the plastic surface and spatially associated with iron, while X-ray absorption spectroscopy indicated its occurrence in ferrihydrite-like phases or as chromite. Although detailed spectroscopic evidence was obtained from a single selected particle, the widespread occurrence of PCF-derived microplastics and their observed metal enrichment suggest that similar geochemical processes may occur at other coastal sites. By linking nationwide field observations with process-level characterization, this study shows that microplastics have the potential to transition from inert debris to geochemically reactive substrates after coastal deposition.

Correction to “A
Multi-Model Assessment of
the Air Quality and Health Impacts of U.S. Energy Decarbonization”

Microbial
Influence on Corrosive Processes at the
Cast Iron-Bentonite Interface during 3.5 Years of Incubation at 37
and 70 °C
articles.abstract: Abstract Bentonite-based geotechnical barriers constitute currently an integral part of international disposal concepts of high-level radioactive waste in claystone and crystalline rock. Elevated temperature, canister corrosion, and metabolic activity of microorganisms can influence their performance. To study these effects on processes at the cast iron-bentonite interface, microcosms were incubated with two different bentonites (B27 and GMZ-001), synthetic Opalinus Clay pore water with a high water-to-bentonite ratio and cast iron plates at 37 and 70 °C over a period of 3.5 years. No microorganisms or nutrients were added to those naturally occurring in the applied materials. Cast iron surfaces in contact with GMZ-001 bentonite appeared strongly corroded, and secondary layer-like structures formed at both temperatures. Furthermore, an accelerated release of iron into the pore water, H2 generation, and gas pressure build-up were observed. In contrast, incubation with B27 bentonite at 37 °C resulted in less corroded cast iron surfaces covered with iron sulfides, which seemed to passivate the surface and led to lower iron release, H2 generation, and gas pressure build-up. Respective B27 microcosms were dominated by metabolically active sulfate-reducing bacteria that induced iron sulfide formation. This study shows that the corrosion behavior of cast iron and changes in geochemical parameters like pH and pore water composition depend on the applied bentonite, naturally occurring microorganisms, and temperature.

articles.title:
Energy
Supply and Demand Coordination Can Advance
Both Climate Goals and Sustainable Development in the Global South
articles.abstract: Abstract Reconciling climate mitigation with sustainable development is a critical imperative in the Global South, where rising emissions coincide with persistent development deficits. Here, we develop an integrated assessment framework linking nationally determined contribution (NDC)-aligned supply-side, demand-side, and coordinated supply–demand policy packages to greenhouse-gas trajectories and a six-goal Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) scorecard. We show that supply-focused renewable expansion or demand-focused efficiency improves selected SDG-related dimensions but creates trade-offs involving energy-cost pressure, water use, and ecosystem protection. By comparison, an integrated supply–demand strategy maximizes the SDG score (69 versus 65 under REF in 2050), enhances clean-energy penetration and efficiency, and averts approximately 485,000 annual premature deaths in 2050 relative to REF. These findings highlight the potential of coordinated supply–demand strategies to reduce climate–SDG trade-offs across the Global South.

articles.title:
Building-Stock
Turnover Reshapes Mitigation Priorities
in China’s Building Sector
articles.abstract: Abstract China’s building sector is pivotal to the 2060 carbon-neutrality ambition, yet prospective assessments often insufficiently capture regional heterogeneity and life-cycle emission dynamics. Here, we develop a provincial-level dynamic framework integrating material flow analysis, life-cycle assessment, and machine-learning-informed parameter trajectories to project emissions through 2060. Under a business-as-usual (BAU) scenario, China’s building life-cycle emissions are projected to peak in 2031–2033, while carbon neutrality remains challenged by persistent pressures from both material use and building operations. These pressures arise from the existing stock, whose continued use sustains energy demand while increasing building retirements shift construction from stock growth to the replacement of retired buildings. Implementing a high-efficiency scenario with regionally differentiated deployment of material- and energy-efficiency strategies could reduce China’s building-sector life-cycle emissions by 90% in 2060 relative to the BAU scenario. Provincial analysis further reveals that similar overall mitigation potential masks substantial differences in the composition of effective mitigation portfolios, reflecting local building-stock and energy-use characteristics. To close the remaining gap, deeper operational decarbonization should be coupled with stock-management strategies that extend building lifetimes, avoid premature demolition, and prioritize renovation and reuse.
